OFFICIAL REPORT
In the Two Hundred and Thirty Seventh Session of the Rajya Sabha commencing 
on the 26th November, 2015/5th Agrahayana, 1937 (Saka)

RAJYA SABHA
Thursday, the 26th November, 2015/5th Agrahayana, 1937 (Saka)
The House met at eleven of the clock,  
MR. CHAIRMAN  in the Chair.
(The National Anthem, "Jana Gana Mana", was played.)
OBITUARY REFERENCES
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing 
away of Prof. Ram Kapse, Dr. Rudra Pratap Singh, Shri N. Rajendran, former 
Members of this House and Shri Khekiho Zhimomi, a sitting Member of this House.
Prof. Ram Kapse passed away on the 29th of September, 2015, at the age of 
81 years.
Born in December, 1933 in Nasik district of Maharashtra, Prof. Ram Kapse was 
educated at the D. G. Ruparel College and the Mumbai University.
A lecturer by profession, Prof. Kapse was associated with several educational 
institutions, library and literary associations. He worked tirelessly for the welfare of 
children and promotion of cooperative housing. He served as the Chairman of the 
City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra (CIDCO) from 1979 
to 1980. He was also a Member of the Municipal Council, Kalyan, Maharashtra, 
from 1962 to 1974.
Prof. Ram Kapse started his legislative career as a Member of the Maharashtra 
Legislative Assembly in 1978 and was a Member of that Assembly for three consecutive 
terms, that is, from 1978 to 1980, from 1980 to 1985 and again from 1985 to 1989. 
He was a Member of the Ninth and the Tenth Lok Sabha. He also served as the 
Chairman of the Committee on Food, Civil Supplies and Public Distribution from 
1993 to 1994.
Prof. Ram Kapse represented the State of Maharashtra in this House from 
September, 1996 to July, 1998.
Prof. Ram Kapse also served as the Lieutenant Governor of Andaman and Nicobar 
Islands from January, 2004 to May, 2006.

2 Obituary  [RAJYA SABHA] References
In the passing away of Prof. Ram Kapse, the country has lost a distinguished 
parliamentarian, an able administrator and a dedicated social worker.
Dr. Rudra Pratap Singh passed away on the 8th of October, 2015, at the age 
of 79 years.
Born in May, 1936 in Sultanpur district of Uttar Pradesh, Dr. Rudra Pratap Singh 
was educated at the Universities of Allahabad and Lucknow.
An agriculturist, Dr. Singh was also a research scholar in Hindi literature and 
actively engaged in the fields of social reforms, national integration and world peace. 
He served as President of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Federation from 1984 to 
1985. He also served on the Committee on Official Language as its Vice-Chairman 
from 1982 to 1986, and as its Deputy Chairman from 1986 to 1992. He was a 
member of the Court of Jawaharlal Nehru University from 1980 to 1984. Dr. Singh 
was a Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly from 1962 to 1967 and of 
the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council from 1967 to 1971. He was also a Member 
of the Fifth Lok Sabha from 1971 to 1977.
Dr. Rudra Pratap Singh represented the State of Uttar Pradesh in this House 
for two consecutive terms from July, 1980 to July, 1986 and again from July, 1986 
to July, 1992. 
In the passing away of Dr. Rudra Pratap Singh, the country has lost a distinguished 
parliamentarian and a dedicated social worker.
Shri N. Rajendran passed away on the 11th of November, 2015, at the age of 
61 years.
Born in May, 1954, in Kovilpatti of Tamil Nadu, Shri Rajendran was educated 
at the V .O.C. Board High School in Kovilpatti.
An agriculturist by vocation, Shri Rajendran was actively involved in various 
social welfare activities. He served as the Chairman of the Kovilpatti Panchayat 
Union from 1986 to 1991.
Shri N. Rajendran represented the State of Tamil Nadu in this House from July, 
1995 to July, 2001.
In the passing away of Shri N. Rajendran, the country has lost an able 
parliamentarian and a dedicated social worker. 
Shri Khekiho Zhimomi passed away today, the 26th of November, 2015, at the 
age of 69 years.

Obituary  [26 November, 2015]  References 3
 Born in February, 1946, in District Zunheboto in Nagaland, Shri Khekiho 
Zhimomi was an active social worker, who strived for the upliftment of the weaker 
and downtrodden sections of society. He was a member of the Court of Nagaland 
University.
Shri Zhimomi started his legislative career as a Member of the Nagaland 
Legislative Assembly in 1989 and served as a Member of that Assembly for three 
terms, i.e., from 1989 to 1992, from 1993 to 1997, and again from 2003 to 2008. 
He also served as Cabinet Minister of Industry and Commerce from 1989 to 1992 
and from 2003 to 2007 and as Cabinet Minister holding the portfolios of Geology, 
Mining and Border Affairs from 2003 to 2007 in the Government of Nagaland.
Shri Khekiho Zhimomi represented the State of Nagaland in this House for two 
terms — from July, 2008 to April, 2010, and from April, 2010 till his sad demise.
In the passing away of Shri Khekiho Zhimomi, the country has lost a distinguished 
parliamentarian, an able administrator and a dedicated social worker.
We deeply mourn the passing away of Prof. Ram Kapse, Dr. Rudra Pratap Singh, 
Shri N. Rajendran and Shri Khekiho Zhimomi. I request Members to rise in their 
places and observe silence as a mark of respect to the memory of the departed.
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members of the bereaved 
families our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy.
As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri Khekiho Zhimomi, a sitting Member, 
the House stands adjourned till 11.00 a.m. on Friday, the 27th of November, 2015.
